facts.text: Bloomington, Idaho, was first settled in April 1864 by Mormon pioneers from Cache Valley, Utah, as part of the Bear Lake Valley colonization.
The town’s name was chosen after a bountiful harvest, echoing Bloomington, Illinois, and highlighting its early agricultural focus.
During its first winter of 1864–1865, deep snow, blizzards, and crop failures tested the resolve of about 41 founding families.
Preservation efforts in the 20th century kept many late‑1800s homes intact, giving Bloomington a distinctive pioneer‑era architectural character.
Bloomington is governed by a mayor‑council system, with Mayor Roy Bunderson overseeing services while preserving its pioneer heritage.
Bloomington sits in the Bear Lake Valley near the Utah border, offering easy access to the lake’s recreational opportunities.
